author: Kathy Belcher
title: Cold Wax and Oil Artist
paragraph1: About the Artist A lifelong learner, explorer and crafter with experience across a range of media – including fabrics, inks, acrylic, paper, watercolor and, most recently, oil and cold wax. My journey into cold wax and oils began in February 2020 during a vacation class, and the subsequent year and a half in Covid quarantine provided invaluable time to research and further explore the medium. Although I came to painting late in life, I have expanded my skills through workshops, Beverly Street Studio School and online classes, continually striving to grow as an artist.
paragraph2: Artistic Process and Materials Each of my artworks begins with three distinctly colored base layers of cold wax and oil, which add vibrancy and depth and serve as a foundation for scratching and mark making. I paint on Arches Oil Paper, later mounting it with archival medium onto a hard-surfaced panel board. The rigid support prevents movement of the paint layers and helps avoid cracking. I apply my paints using tools like squeegees and palette knives rather than brushes. Every piece receives at least two final layers of pure cold wax to protect its surface, resulting in works that are truly one of a kind.
paragraph3: Inspiration and Artistic Approach As an artist who mainly works with oil and cold wax, I focus on creating landscapes that celebrate the beauty and wonder of nature. In my paintings, I use abstraction to blur familiar shapes, letting forms appear and disappear so viewers can interpret the scene in their own way. This approach helps create an intimate connection where each person's story weaves together with my artistic vision. Color plays a vital role in my work. I use bold hues to inspire emotion and depth. My goal is to capture feelings of love and familiarity found in everyday life, inviting viewers to notice overlooked beauty and form their own connections through these abstract pieces.
paragraph4: Continuous Growth and Exploration I am constantly challenging myself to try new painting styles and techniques, appreciating how the slow drying time lets me explore, revise and fully develop my ideas. I often work on a series of paintings, returning to earlier pieces after a few hours or days to add more layers. Some days, I am captivated by a particular color statement; on others, I am drawn to arranging intriguing textures.

author: Kathy Belcher
title: Bio
paragraph1: Creating art for me is a form of meditation. When a landscape painting is going well, it is not so much about the image for me; it is about being with the painting, inside the painting space. I often get lost in my work, losing a sense of time and specific space. My contemporary semi-abstract paintings give the viewer the opportunity to travel to a place of peace and tranquility.
paragraph2: Kathy’s use of color affords her unlimited freedom to create on her canvas a world beyond, one seemingly untouched.  Impressionistic in style, her landscapes invite the viewer in, but allow each one to draw his own conclusion.
paragraph3: “Paintings are as much about the paint as they are about the subject matter,” explains the artist.  Rather than seeing a photograph, Kathy would like the viewer to “connect” with the painting, to share in a visual language embracing the underlying emotions experienced as she orchestrated each piece.
paragraph4: The composition: most often the pastoral countryside's of Virginia under a shroud of unorthodox color, echoing simplicity and placidness found in our natural surroundings.
paragraph5: From moody to brilliant, Kathy’s use of color affords her unlimited freedom to create on her canvas a world beyond, one seemingly untouched.  Impressionistic in style, his landscapes invite the viewer in, but allow each one to draw his own conclusion.
paragraph6: “Paintings are as much about the paint as they are about the subject matter,” explains the artist.  Rather than seeing a photograph, Kathy would like the viewer to “connect” with the painting, to share in a visual language embracing the underlying emotions experienced as she orchestrated each piece.
paragraph7: I paint for the pleasure of working with oil colors - their luminosity and complexity, the messiness of mixing them and moving them around on a canvas - and for the challenge of the decision making process of painting.
paragraph8: I love the experience of looking intently at a chosen subject while I paint to make a personal connection with it.  I may discover a significant detail that I initially missed, find new relationships between elements of the subject which enhance its meaning or unity, or develop new ideas about what I want the painting to say.  I enjoy the adventure of beginning a new painting and working to convey my sensory experience of the subject to the viewer.
